title: Polygon Area From Coordinates in Acres
description: Compute the area enclosed by a coordinate polygon with Polygon Area From Coordinates — square metres, hectares and acres from your corners. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a four-point polygon over Midtown Manhattan — corners at 40.7580, −73.9855 and its neighbours — encloses 1.742 km² (430 acres) inside a 5.28 km boundary, all computed from the corners alone.
quick_answer: Polygon Area From Coordinates computes the ground area enclosed by a polygon whose corners are latitude/longitude pairs, using the shoelace method on a locally projected plane. Paste the corners in boundary order and read the area in square metres, hectares and acres — for fields, parcels, sites and zones.

body.t: Corners (40.7580, −73.9855), (40.7580, −73.9700), (40.7700, −73.9700), (40.7700, −73.9855): the enclosed area computes to 1.742 km² — 174.2 hectares, 430.3 acres. The edges run 1.31–1.33 km: a serious city park's worth of ground.

List the same corners crossed (bowtie order) and the shoelace sum cancels itself toward nonsense. The calculator expects a walked boundary — each point the next corner along the fence, never a scatter.
